quiz.0.question: Which international variety is Cannonau genetically identical to?
quiz.0.explanation: Cannonau is the Sardinian name for Grenache/Garnacha. DNA studies suggest Sardinia may actually be the grape's original homeland — predating its cultivation in Spain and France.
quiz.1.question: What makes Vermentino di Gallura DOCG special?
quiz.1.options.0: It is Sardinia's only red wine DOCG
quiz.1.options.1: It is the only DOCG in Sardinia and southern Italy for a white wine — grown on ancient granite soils
quiz.1.options.2: It is made using the Metodo Classico
quiz.1.options.3: It must be aged for a minimum of 10 years
quiz.1.explanation: Vermentino di Gallura DOCG is noteworthy as the only DOCG in Sardinia and one of very few white wine DOCGs in southern Italy — grown on the ancient granite soils of northern Sardinia (Gallura).
quiz.2.question: What is distinctive about Carignano del Sulcis?
quiz.2.options.0: It is made from international varieties only
quiz.2.options.1: Many vines are ungrafted, pre-phylloxera, planted in sandy soils — some over 100 years old
quiz.2.options.2: It is always made as a sparkling wine
quiz.2.options.3: It can only be made as a sweet wine
quiz.2.explanation: The Sulcis area's sandy soils protected vines from phylloxera, so many Carignano del Sulcis vines are old, ungrafted (on their own roots) — producing extraordinarily concentrated wines.
quiz.3.question: What is Bottarga?
quiz.3.options.1: Cured, salted and dried mullet or tuna roe — Sardinia's 'Mediterranean caviar'
quiz.3.options.2: A sheep's milk cheese from Sardinia
quiz.3.explanation: Bottarga — cured, dried mullet roe — is one of Sardinia's most prized food products, used grated over pasta or eaten in thin slices. It pairs magnificently with Vermentino di Gallura.
